subject: Tilt Commerce — questions on regional data affinity, retention, and erasure (hosted API)
messages:
From: Anya Petrov <anya@tiltcommerce.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Tilt Commerce Security <security@tiltcommerce.com>, Raj Patel <raj@tiltcommerce.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Questions: regional data affinity + retention windows for hosted API

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — Tilt is keen to validate operational controls before we move to a pilot. Security has a short questionnaire focused on data residency and lifecycle for the hosted API. Two asks we need clear answers on:

1) Can customer requests be pinned to a geographic region (US-East / EU-West)? If yes, is it enforced at the tenant level or only at routing preference?
2) For tenant deletion/erasure requests: what is the end-to-end timeline (from API request to complete removal from primary store, caches, backups), and how do you demonstrate completion?
3) What retention windows apply to system-level backups and logs that may contain customer identifiers?

Could you respond with the short-form answers plus any evidence or artifacts (dataflow diagram, retention matrix, sample audit log / erasure attestation)? We need something we can attach to our procurement packet.

Appreciate a response by end of week if possible.

Best,
Anya
Security Program Manager, Tilt Commerce

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@tiltcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions: regional data affinity + retention windows for hosted API

Hi Anya — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Ben (sales engineer) and Rishi (security) so you get both an operational answer and the evidence pack. Short answers below; see attachments for diagrams and a retention matrix.

1) Region pinning: Yes. We provide tenant-level region affinity that is enforced at the request routing layer and validated by the control plane during provisioning. For most customers we offer a region pin (US-East, US-West, EU-West) at onboarding; we also support an explicit per-request region header if customers opt into cross-region routing.

2) Tenant erasure timeline: Typical flow is:
  - API initiated erasure request acknowledged immediately (0 minutes)
  - Primary datastore deletion and KV cache eviction: completed within 24 hours for active shards
  - Propagation to downstream caches/replicas: up to 72 hours in high-availability configurations
  - Backup retention window: backups are retained for 30 days by default (can be shortened via enterprise addendum) and subject to a purge schedule described in the attachment
  - Final attestations and audit log entry generated within 5 business days once the background purge completes

3) System backups & logs: Production backups are encrypted-at-rest and stored with a default 30-day retention. Audit logs (access and admin actions) are retained for 90 days in the standard plan; longer retention is available as an add-on. We provide UI + API endpoints to request export of matching audit entries for a given erasure request.

Attached: redwood-hostedapi-data-retention-summary.pdf, data-retention-matrix.csv, hostedapi-dataflow-diagram.png

If you want, Rishi can provide a short attestation template we sign once the erasure completes.

Let us know the procurement timeline and any clause language Tilt needs in the contract.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions: regional data affinity + retention windows for hosted API

Hi Anya — adding some implementation-level details that customers often ask for when they evaluate the hosted path.

Region enforcement: traffic is routed by the control plane to regional serving pools. Tenant region affinity is enforced by (1) a tenant metadata flag at provision time and (2) a runtime check in the router that rejects requests lacking the correct region header when a strict region policy is enabled. We maintain signed routing logs for 180 days for forensic needs (these are separate from audit logs).

Erasure mechanics: for performance we have two caches — per-request KV cache and prefix cache. An erasure trigger deletes primary records and sends an invalidation message to both cache layers. Because of eventual consistency between replicas, we do conservatively hold a small window (<=72 hours) before marking the erasure complete in the system UI. If Tilt requires accelerated removal from backups, we can map that into a contract-backed SLA and shorten the backup purge window to 7 days; this requires a subscription addendum.

Evidence we can provide:
- Signed erasure attestation (PDF)
- Per-tenant purge log extract (CSV)
- Host-level snapshot manifest showing post-erasure snapshot indexes (redacted)

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the diagrams.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions: regional data affinity + retention windows for hosted API

Anya — quick security confirmation and a few compliance notes.

Summary answers:
- Data residency controls: Tenant-level region pinning is enforced. We also support contractually binding geo-fencing for EU-only data processing; this includes restricted staff access and region-scoped backups.
- Erasure: We can certify deletion from primary stores and caches within 72 hours and provide a signed attestation once background backup purges complete (default 30-day backup retention).
- Auditability: Each erasure request generates a unique job id. All state transitions (request received, primary delete, cache invalidation, backup purge scheduled, attestation issued) are recorded in the audit trail. Audit exports can be delivered as CSV or uploaded to a customer S3 with a pre-signed URL.

Controls & mitigations:
- Backups are immutably versioned; purge jobs are audited and run under a documented schedule. For regulated customers we operate a backup-erase playbook that includes manual verification steps and a secondary audit by the security operations team.
- We provide role-based access control (RBAC) in the console; only authorized Ops/SRE staff (audited) can run manual purge jobs.
- For legal hold scenarios we support freeze operations; customers can request a freeze that temporarily prevents deletion while the hold is active.

Attachments included in this thread are the artifacts we normally share with procurement: a short retention summary, a matrix mapping data types to retention windows, and a high-level dataflow diagram. If Tilt needs, we can generate a one-off backup manifest and coordinate a secure transfer.

I can also prepare a short attestation template for erasure completion if you want us to sign. Tell me what format Tilt prefers (PDF + signature or a letter on company letterhead).

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
